:::{#thm-dot-linear}
#### The dot product is linear in each slot

For vectors $\vecf{x}, \vecf{u}, \vecf{w} \in \reals^p$ and numbers $a, b$,

$$
\vecf{x} \cdot (a\,\vecf{u} + b\,\vecf{w})
= a\,(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{u}) + b\,(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{w})
$$

and

$$
(a\,\vecf{u} + b\,\vecf{w}) \cdot \vecf{x}
= a\,(\vecf{u} \cdot \vecf{x}) + b\,(\vecf{w} \cdot \vecf{x}).
$$

:::

::: proof

**Second slot.**

$$
\ba
\vecf{x} \cdot (a\,\vecf{u} + b\,\vecf{w})
&= \sumip x_i\,(a\,\vecf{u} + b\,\vecf{w})_i
&& \text{(@def-dot-product)}
\\
&= \sumip x_i\,(a u_i + b w_i)
&& \text{(@def-scalar-mult, @def-vector-addition)}
\\
&= \sumip \paren{x_i a u_i + x_i b w_i}
&& \text{(distribute each } x_i \text{)}
\\
&= \sumip \paren{a\,x_i u_i + b\,x_i w_i}
&& \text{(commute the factors in each product)}
\\
&= \sumip a\,x_i u_i + \sumip b\,x_i w_i
&& \text{(split the finite sum)}
\\
&= a \sumip x_i u_i + b \sumip x_i w_i
&& \text{(factor } a \text{ and } b \text{ out of the sums)}
\\
&= a\,(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{u}) + b\,(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{w}).
&& \text{(@def-dot-product)}
\ea
$$

**First slot.**

$$
\ba
(a\,\vecf{u} + b\,\vecf{w}) \cdot \vecf{x}
&= \vecf{x} \cdot (a\,\vecf{u} + b\,\vecf{w})
&& \text{(@thm-lincom-symmetric)}
\\
&= a\,(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{u}) + b\,(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{w})
&& \text{(second slot)}
\\
&= a\,(\vecf{u} \cdot \vecf{x}) + b\,(\vecf{w} \cdot \vecf{x}).
&& \text{(@thm-lincom-symmetric, twice)}
\ea
$$

Two special cases are used often.
With $a = b = 1$, and $1\,\vecf{u} = \vecf{u}$,
the theorem gives $\vecf{x} \cdot (\vecf{u} + \vecf{w}) = \vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{u} + \vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{w}$.
With $\vecf{w} = \vecf{u}$ and $b = 0$, and $0\,\vecf{u} = \vzero$,
it gives $\vecf{x} \cdot (a\,\vecf{u}) = a\,(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{u})$,
and likewise in the first slot.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-dot-linear}
#### Splitting a dot product

Let $\vecf{x} = (1, 2)$, $\vecf{u} = (3, 0)$, $\vecf{w} = (0, 1)$, $a = 2$ and $b = -1$.
Directly,
$a\,\vecf{u} + b\,\vecf{w} = (6, -1)$
and $\vecf{x} \cdot (6, -1) = 6 - 2 = 4$.
By @thm-dot-linear,
$a\,(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{u}) + b\,(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{w}) = 2 \cd 3 + (-1) \cd 2 = 4$,
the same number.

:::
